title: Backcompat adapter for embeddings + rerank: cursor translation, error mapping, and streaming framing
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Design and deliver a backward-compatibility adapter layer that allows legacy embed/rerank clients to call the new unified embeddings+rerank endpoints without breaking pagination semantics or error-handling expectations. The adapter translates legacy cursor tokens to the new cursor encoding, normalizes HTTP error codes and bodies to legacy contracts, and preserves streaming framing and structured-output shapes expected by older SDKs.
background: Recent launches consolidated multiple embeddings and rerank endpoints into a unified service that uses a new cursor_v2 token and returns richer structured outputs and streaming frames. Several enterprise customers (and internal production clients) still use older SDKs and clients that expect: 1) cursor-based pagination using 'next_token' style opaque strings, 2) specific HTTP mapping for transient vs permanent errors, and 3) legacy streaming frame formats for incremental rerank results. Breaking them caused multiple support tickets and a stalled Dedicated rollout. We need an adapter that preserves the legacy contract while allowing internal evolution of the unified API.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy clients can page through embeddings + rerank results using their existing SDKs without code changes
Adapter returns exactly the legacy error codes and JSON error shape for mapped cases (see mapping table in technical_notes)
Cursor tokens issued by adapter are compatible with both legacy and new clients for the transition window
End-to-end regression tests for pagination edge cases (duplicate items across pages, out-of-order inserts, cursor TTL) pass in CI
Streaming rerank results from unified service are converted into legacy SSE/HTTP-stream frames with no more than 50ms additional tail latency in the adapter under p95 load
Telemetry emits a compatibility-migration metric with counts of legacy vs native tokens per customer
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Internal Canary: deploy adapter in front of unified endpoint in staging and route 5% of internal test accounts
Phase 2 - Controlled Beta: enable adapter for select enterprise customers behind feature flag and run for 2 weeks
Phase 3 - Gradual Production: ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% for legacy-versioned clients with monitoring thresholds
Phase 4 - Deprecation Notice: when adoption metric shows <1% legacy token issuance for 90 days, schedule deprecation RFC and customer notices
decisions: Adapter will be implemented as a thin layer in the control plane (stateless when possible) to avoid per-request state scaling issues
Cursor translation will be deterministic and reversible for a migration window: adapter keeps a short-lived signed mapping so old tokens can be resolved to cursor_v2 and vice versa
We will not attempt to retroactively reorder results: adapter preserves ordering from the unified service and documents differences where legacy clients assumed stable sorting beyond guarantee
Streaming adapter semantics: prefer pass-through to minimize latency; only reframe events when necessary for legacy clients
Default Retry-After behavior: adapter will copy Retry-After from origin if present; otherwise map transient rate limits to 30s when returning 429 to legacy clients
technical_notes: Cursor translation approach: issue adapter-scoped tokens that embed (base64) an HMAC-signed payload containing the underlying cursor_v2 plus a version tag and expiry. This allows stateless verification but enables revocation by rotating signing keys

Error mapping (summary): origin 429 -> 429 (preserve Retry-After header when present); origin 503/504 -> 503 with legacy body {"error": {"type": "temporary", "message": ...}}; origin 400-range model validation errors -> 400 with legacy validation code; origin 500 -> 502 for legacy clients to encourage retrying via client SDKs

Streaming framing: unified service uses protobuf-chunked frames. Adapter will expose legacy SSE with event: "rerank" lines converting proto payload to legacy JSON schema. Binary blobs (embeddings) will be base64 encoded when streaming to legacy clients

Partial results: when unified service returns partial/best-effort results with a retry token, adapter will include legacy-compatible 'partial: true' field and surface a migration warning in the response body
Idempotency and dedup: adapter will surface an 'adapter_request_id' header for troubleshooting and to help clients deduplicate when they re-play requests
Performance SLO: adapter should add <5% CPU overhead and <50ms p95 added latency at typical qps. Perf tests will be automated in infra pipeline
tasks: Write adapter design doc and get cross-functional sign-off (PM/Eng/SRE/Security)
Implement adapter service with cursor translation and error-mapping modules
Add streaming reframe module to convert proto frames to SSE for legacy clients
Create regression test harness: legacy SDK runner + randomized pagination fuzzing
Instrument telemetry and create dashboard for legacy-token usage and adapter error rates
Run canary and measure latency/cost impact; iterate on batching/caching in adapter
Prepare customer migration playbook and support runbook

incident_learnings: Do not change cursor semantics without a mapping layer; several production clients resumed after rolling adapter back
Implicit assumptions in older SDKs (stable deterministic sort across model variants) must be surfaced in docs; adapter cannot guarantee those properties
Monitoring around token conversions quickly reveals client-side version skew; expose metrics per-customer to drive migration outreach
